title: Test runs leak ward-packaged-* build dirs into TMPDIR (~1.1 GiB/hour on minim4)
summary: test/support/packaged.ts never removes its mkdtemp build root under bun test; minim4 filled to critical low disk.
description: Found by the remote-mgmt fleet session on 2026-09-29 while diagnosing minim4 running out of disk (critical low-disk event at 04:36). $TMPDIR held 146 ward-packaged-* dirs, 17.1 GiB, all created since 2026-09-28 17:00, at a steady ~8-14 per hour (~1.1 GiB/hour), each ~117 MB with env-probe/ and ward/ inside. Cause: test/support/packaged.ts:9-10 creates buildRoot = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "ward-packaged-")) at module load and removes it only in process.on("exit"). Under bun test, and in the crash-style fixtures (vault-store-worker.ts crash/crash-create), that handler evidently never runs. minim4 has 29 GiB free, so at this rate the boot disk fills in about a day. The remote-mgmt session is deleting leftovers older than 2 h, but they come back until this is fixed.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A full test run leaves no ward-packaged-* directory in TMPDIR (verified by listing TMPDIR before and after)

Cleanup does not depend on process exit (removal registered in afterAll rather than at process exit), and reclamation of stale residue is the explicit `bun run clean:temp` (ADR 0013), which no test run, hook, or CI job invokes
Crash-style tests (vault-store-worker crash/crash-create) also leave nothing behind in TMPDIR (ward-store-* included)

plan: 1. Create the temporary root through one shared helper: sweep stale ward-* roots older than two hours at creation, and remove the root in an afterAll so cleanup does not depend on reaching the exit handlers.
2. Move the three roots named by the criteria onto it: the packaged build root (two 63 MB binaries per importing file), the launcher work root, and the vault-store root the crash fixtures use.
3. Measure the two criteria rather than infer them: no ward-packaged-* or ward-store-* root left after a full run, and a planted stale root swept while a fresh one survives.
implementationNotes:
FIXED 2026-09-29, in this pull request, with one criterion deliberately left unmet and recorded rather than faked.

WHAT LANDED. test/support/temp-root.ts is now the one way a test file makes a temporary root: it creates the directory and registers its removal in an afterAll, so cleanup runs at the end of the importing file's own tests instead of waiting for the process to reach its exit handlers. Measured before the change was written, because the design rested on it: a support module CAN register that hook from module scope and it does run for the importing file - three consecutive runs of a probe file left nothing behind.

A SECOND DEFECT THE FIRST ATTEMPT INTRODUCED, found by running the suite rather than by reasoning. A root created in the shared support module belongs to whichever file imports it FIRST, because bun test evaluates that module once for the whole process: with the packaged root created there and its removal registered by the first file, the second file's tests failed with ENOENT on the binary - measured, one evaluation for two importing files, and 18 failures in non-disclosure.test.ts. The build root is therefore owned by the calling file, one per file, which also matches how every other test file in this suite already creates its root. A second build costs 0.27 s (bundle 7 ms, compile 254 ms), so nothing was traded for it.

THREE FILES MOVED ONTO IT, plus one the measurement found rather than the report:
- test/support/packaged.ts (the ~122 MB root: two compiled binaries),
- test/launcher.test.ts (its work area and both binaries now share one root),
- test/vault-store.test.ts (the root the crash fixtures write under),
- test/lore-agent-sources.test.ts, which created a stub directory and removed it NOWHERE - it leaked one directory on every run, which no criterion named and the before/after listing found,
- test/fixtures/setup-exit-probe.ts now makes its directory under the caller's working directory rather than under TMPDIR, so the parent that spawned it reclaims it: this is the process that must not be waited on, so nothing in it can clean up after itself.

MEASURED (AC1), listing TMPDIR before and after a full run - 667 pass, 0 fail, 3 pre-existing lint warnings, layer check 0 violations: every family unchanged. ward-packaged 183 before and 183 after, ward-lore 119 and 119, ward-exit 197 and 197, ward-store, ward-launcher and ward-setup unchanged. The run leaves nothing of its own. (The counts are not zero because 871 roots from earlier killed runs and older code are still there; that is the residue the unmet criterion below is about.)

NOT IMPLEMENTED, and this is the criterion left unmet (AC2's second half): the start-of-run sweep of stale roots older than a few hours. It is a recursive delete of age-filtered directories out of a shared TMPDIR, and the permission layer refused it the first time the helper exercised it, which is the right call for a capability no user has authorised - a test helper is not the place to add destructive cleanup of a shared scratch directory. The first half of the criterion, cleanup that does not depend on process exit, is implemented and measured. The remaining question goes to this repository's own user; the repair for the disk that started this task is already in: normal runs no longer add to it, and the fleet session on minim4 is already sweeping what killed runs leave.

ROUTING CORRECTED, 2026-09-29, on opum-agent's instruction and before any answer arrived: the sweep question does NOT go to this repository's pane user, because nobody reads that pane and a question there waits for no one. It goes to opum-agent as an A/B with the exact action, the refusal, a recommendation and the alternative; the orchestrator routes it, and if the action is tier 3 it reaches the operator as a dialog in this session. The note above says otherwise and is left as written rather than edited, because it records what was done at the time; this note is the correction, and the criterion remains unchecked either way.

HANDOFF, 2026-09-29, session recycled on budget. State stays In Progress with one criterion honestly unchecked.

LANDED, as opum-ai/ward-cli#120: every temporary root a test file makes now comes from test/support/temp-root.ts, which registers its removal in that file's own afterAll, so cleanup no longer waits for the process to reach its exit handlers. Measured before and after a full run - ward-packaged 183 either side, ward-lore 119, ward-exit 197, the rest unchanged - and the same measurement found two leakers no criterion had named, a stub directory in test/lore-agent-sources.test.ts that was removed nowhere and the setup exit probe's directory, both fixed in the same change.

STILL OPEN, the only thing left: AC2's second half, the start-of-run sweep of stale ward-* roots. It is with the operator as DEC-49, asked as an A/B: A, ship an explicit `bun run clean:temp` that a person or CI runs deliberately and never let a test run delete directories it did not create; or B, the literal sweep in the helper, which reclaims residue automatically and means every test run deletes age-filtered directories it did not create. My recommendation is A. The permission layer refused the action the first time the helper exercised it, which is why this is a person's call and not a test helper's - that refusal is the evidence, not an obstacle to route around. The criterion stays unchecked until the answer, and it is not blocked on anything else: the first half of it is done and measured.

WHAT REMAINS EITHER WAY: 871 stale ward-* roots, about 21 GiB, are sitting in this machine's TMPDIR as residue from runs that were killed; nothing reclaims them until the answer, and the fleet session on minim4 continues to sweep its own by hand at two hours.

CLOSED 2026-09-29 (this pull request). AC2 amended here rather than checked against its withdrawn sweep clause; the original sweep half is preserved in ADR 0013. What landed: scripts/clean-temp.mjs and `bun run clean:temp` (prefix ward-, real directories only, 120-minute default, --older-than-minutes, --dry-run, and a summary that reports what was scanned as well as what was removed), 7 cases in test/clean-temp.test.ts through a fixture TMPDIR, and ADR 0013 with the operator answer verbatim. Evidence: bun run check green on 7a5fbbb (685 pass, 0 fail); the dry run against this machine real TMPDIR read 70,529 entries, 869 ward-* directories, 724 older than 120 minutes; the command is absent from bun run check and CI, and its only spawn is the test own, pointed at a fixture. The reclaiming run itself is deliberately left to a person: destructive cleanup of a shared TMPDIR stays with the user.
finalSummary: Delivered in opum-ai/ward-cli#127. The run that validated the deliverable is 36601386004 on 7a5fbbb (Check, Docs, Tracker integrity all green); the tracker-only commit that follows it is covered by the merge gate. AC2 was amended to the DEC-49 shape and checked: cleanup no longer depends on process exit (PR #120), and reclamation is the explicit `bun run clean:temp` (ADR 0013), invoked by nothing but a person or a deliberate step. Closed with every criterion checked.
